sourcedFrom: BANISH BACKCOUNTRY — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED (NOT PRINTED)
cleanIntro: A hunting can built for weight: 5.5 inches and 7.8 oz of titanium without its mount, 5.7 inches and 9.0 oz with it, rated up to 300 RUM on a Direct Thread Universal Hub. ⛔ It is FULLY WELDED. Six baffles are named in the specs — five baffles and one accuracy baffle — but none of them come out, and the only component that detaches is the mount interface. A muzzle brake also cannot be fitted to it directly; that needs a secondary attachment sold separately.

steps.title: Clear the host, using the host's own manual
steps.action: Unload the rifle and open the action so the chamber is visibly clear before the can is disturbed. Banish prints no clearing procedure and sends you to your own firearm's manual — appropriate for a hunting can that lives on bolt guns of several actions.
steps.prose: In the field this is the step most likely to be skipped because the can is coming off at the truck. Do it anyway.
steps.quote: If you are at all unsure as to the proper procedures to ensure that your firearm is unloaded, please consult your firearm user’s manual/instructions and/or contact a properly licensed dealer or the manufacturer of your firearm.
steps.cite: BANISH BACKCOUNTRY — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — WARNING, p.2
steps.warn: The host firearm's manual is the clearing authority.

steps.title: Backcountry ceiling — up to 300 RUM
steps.action: Match the host cartridge to the rating. The SPECS block gives CALIBER .300 and CALIBER RANGE Up to 300 RUM, with a 5/8x24 thread pitch and titanium construction. Banish's own published at-ear figures are 135 dB for .308 WIN, 137 dB for 300 Win Mag and 138 dB for 300 RUM, all measured on 20 inch barrels.
steps.prose: Those numbers are worth reading as a set: this is a light can and it gets louder as the cartridge gets bigger. The 300 RUM figure is the ceiling in both senses.
steps.quote: Testing shows that the Banish Backcountry has an average, at ear, meter reading of 135 dB for .308 WIN, 137 dB for 300 Win Mag, and 138 dB for 300 RUM, all configured with 20” barrels.
steps.cite: BANISH BACKCOUNTRY — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — SPECS, p.3
steps.warn: Up to 300 RUM. Hearing protection at every one of those levels.

steps.title: ⛔ Not user-serviceable — the can is fully welded
steps.action: Do not look for a way in. Banish states the Backcountry is fully welded and the baffles cannot be removed; the only part that can be taken off for cleaning is the mount interface. There is no end cap, no baffle removal tool and no internal torque figure in this book, because none of those things exist for this can.
steps.prose: The SPECS line reads SELF-SERVICE: NO. The six baffles the specs name — five plus one accuracy baffle — are described so you know what is inside, not so you can take them out.
steps.quote: The BANISH Backcountry is not user-serviceable, meaning it is fully welded and the baffles cannot be removed. The only part that can be removed for cleaning is the mount interface.
steps.cite: BANISH BACKCOUNTRY — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — CLEANING, p.7
steps.warn: Welded can. There is no teardown.

steps.title: ⛔ The mount goes into the can first, at 50-60 in-lbs
steps.action: Before this can ever meets a barrel, the supplied mount must be threaded into the suppressor and tightened to 50 to 60 in-lbs. That is the joint the whole assembly hangs off, and a can with a loose mount will still thread onto a host and still be off axis.
steps.prose: It is also the one joint you will keep breaking, because Banish requires the mount out for every clean. Torque it back each time; do not leave it hand tight.
steps.quote: Prior to mounting the suppressor to the firearm, you must first thread and tighten the mount (shipped with the suppressor) into the suppressor. Carefully thread the mount into the suppressor and tighten to 50-60 in-lbs.
steps.cite: BANISH BACKCOUNTRY — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — INSTALLATION OF SUPPRESSOR, p.4
steps.warn: 50-60 in-lbs, every time the mount goes back in.

steps.title: ⛔ A muzzle brake needs a secondary attachment on this can
steps.action: Do not try to hang the Backcountry off a brake directly. Banish states that muzzle brakes require a secondary attachment, sold separately, to be able to attach to this suppressor. Out of the box it is a direct thread can on its universal hub mount.
steps.prose: That is a real difference from the 30-GOLD, which ships WITH its brake and mounts to nothing else. The two cans look similar in a catalogue and mount completely differently.
steps.aside: 'to be able to attached' is the publisher's wording.
steps.quote: Muzzle brakes will require a secondary attachment, sold separately, to be able to attached to the BANISH Backcountry.
steps.cite: BANISH BACKCOUNTRY — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — INSTALLATION OF SUPPRESSOR, p.4
steps.warn: No brake mounting without the secondary attachment.

steps.title: Check the seat before firing and before stripping
steps.action: Confirm the thread mount is fully shouldered on the barrel with no visible gap, and that any crush washer left by a previous muzzle device is gone. Banish is blunt about the consequence of a gap: poor accuracy and product damage, and do not fire the host at all.
steps.prose: On a 7.8 oz can the whole point is that you forget it is there. That is exactly why the seat needs a deliberate look each time.
steps.quote: Check the fit between your barrel and silencer before firing! The thread mount must be fully shouldered on the barrel.
steps.cite: BANISH BACKCOUNTRY — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — WARNING, p.2
steps.warn: If there is any gap DO NOT fire the host with the silencer attached.

steps.title: Let it cool, or use a cover
steps.action: After firing, the can is hot enough to burn. Banish tells you to use extreme caution removing it and offers a Devour suppressor cover or gloves. A light titanium can heats faster than a heavy one because there is less metal to absorb the energy.
steps.prose: In cold hunting weather the temptation to grab a warm can is real. It is still 300 RUM heat inside 7.8 oz of titanium.
steps.quote: When removing the silencer, use extreme caution as it may be hot to the touch after firing.
steps.cite: BANISH BACKCOUNTRY — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — WARNING, p.2

steps.title: Take the Backcountry off, then the mount out of the can
steps.action: Unthread the can from the host, then unthread the mount interface out of the back of the can. That mount is the only component that separates, and Banish requires it out for cleaning so all three thread surfaces can be reached — the silencer's own threads and the mount's internal and external threads.
steps.prose: Handle it as a single unit until the mount is out; there is nothing else that can fall off, and nothing else that can be lost.
steps.caution: Three thread surfaces. Clean all three.
steps.quote: Ensure to remove the mount and thoroughly clean the threads of any debris or buildup. This should be done for both the silencer threads, as well as the mount’s internal, and external, threads.
steps.cite: BANISH BACKCOUNTRY — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — CLEANING, p.7

steps.title: Protect the muzzle threads and never fire an obstructed can
steps.action: Cap the bare 5/8x24 threads with a thread protector or another muzzle device for storage and transport, and before the can goes back on, sight through it. Mud and dirt are exactly what a hunting can picks up, and Banish forbids firing through any obstruction.
steps.prose: On a welded can you cannot open it to check, so the sight-through is the whole inspection. Do it in daylight, not at the truck at dusk.
steps.quote: Silencers must be free of obstructions such as mud, dirt, etc. DO NOT attempt to shoot through an obstructed silencer.
steps.cite: BANISH BACKCOUNTRY — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — WARNING, p.2
steps.warn: Look through it. You cannot open it.

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: The Backcountry is off the rifle with its mount out — and that is the entire strip, because the body is welded shut. Banish sets the cleaning interval at every 50 to 100 rounds fired and warns off solid lead or plated lead bullets. Everything beyond this is a soak or a sonic cycle, which the Deep Clean covers.
steps.prose: For a hunting can that fires a handful of rounds a season, that interval will usually mean cleaning it once a year rather than once a range trip.
steps.quote: It is recommended that the suppressor be cleaned every 50 - 100 rounds fired. The use of solid lead or plated lead bullets is not recommended.
steps.cite: BANISH BACKCOUNTRY — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — CLEANING, p.7

deepSteps.title: Sonic wash or a one-to-two day soak
deepSteps.action: With the can off the rifle, put it into a sonic wash for one to two cycles, or soak it in a cleaning solution for one to two days. Any firearm solvent or sonic wash cleaning solution will work. There is nothing to disassemble first — this is done with the can whole.
deepSteps.prose: Note the soak time is measured in DAYS here, not the 24 hours the serviceable Banish cans specify. A welded can has nowhere for the solvent to be helped along.
deepSteps.quote: Place the silencer into a sonic wash for one to two cycles, or soak in a cleaning solution for one to two days.
deepSteps.cite: BANISH BACKCOUNTRY — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — CLEANING, p.7

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Nothing that strips Cerakote
deepSteps.action: Check what is in the tank before the can goes in. Banish forbids solutions that will strip the Cerakote coating. On a hunting can carried in the weather, that finish is the corrosion barrier, and titanium with the coating gone will discolour permanently around the blast chamber.
deepSteps.prose: Many aggressive carbon removers will take Cerakote off. Read the solution's own instructions rather than assuming a gun-cleaning label means safe.
deepSteps.quote: Ensure not to use solutions that will strip the Cerakote coating from the silencer.
deepSteps.cite: BANISH BACKCOUNTRY — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — CLEANING, p.7

deepSteps.title: Brass brush the blast chamber and accuracy baffle
deepSteps.action: Once soaked, work a brass brush over the blast chamber and the accuracy baffle. Those are the two features Banish names and the two you can physically reach from the ends of a welded 5.5 inch can. The other four baffles stay where they are and get cleaned by the soak alone.
deepSteps.prose: Brass, not steel. Titanium galls and scratches easily and there is no way to inspect or repair a scratch you cannot see.
deepSteps.quote: Once soaked, take a brass brush, and clean the blast chamber and accuracy baffle.
deepSteps.cite: BANISH BACKCOUNTRY — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — CLEANING, p.7

deepSteps.title: Dry it, refit the mount, then fire 10-15 rounds
deepSteps.action: Let the suppressor dry completely, re-install the mount at its 50-60 in-lbs, and then fire 10 to 15 rounds. Banish's reasoning is explicit: the high pressure blows out the loose debris and buildup that the cleaning loosened but did not carry away.
deepSteps.prose: On a can you cannot open, that fouling string is the last stage of the cleaning process rather than the first shots of the next outing. Plan for it.
deepSteps.quote: Once clean, allow the suppressor to dry. Re-install the mount and you are ready to shoot again. Shoot 10-15 rounds through the suppressor. The high pressure will shoot out any loose debris and buildup that was loosened during cleaning.
deepSteps.cite: BANISH BACKCOUNTRY — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — CLEANING, p.7
deepSteps.warn: Fully dry before firing — trapped solvent is an obstruction.

cleaning.name: SOAK OR SONIC
tasks: Sonic wash for one to two cycles, OR soak in cleaning solution for one to two days
Any firearm solvent or sonic wash cleaning solution is acceptable
Use nothing that will strip the Cerakote coating
Do not attempt to open the can — it is fully welded

cleaning.name: REACHABLE INTERNALS
tasks: Leave the remaining baffles to the soak; they cannot be removed

cleaning.name: MOUNT AND THREADS
tasks: Remove the mount interface — the only removable component
Clean the mount's internal and external threads
Refit and tighten the mount to 50-60 in-lbs

cleaning.name: AFTER CLEANING
tasks: Fire 10 to 15 rounds to blow out loosened debris
Do not use solid lead or plated lead bullets
Fit a thread protector to the host's 5/8x24 muzzle threads whenever the can is off

reassembly: Confirm the can is completely dry before anything goes back together.
Thread the mount interface into the suppressor and tighten it to 50-60 in-lbs.
Thread the can onto the host's 5/8x24 muzzle and confirm the mount is fully shouldered with no visible gap.
If a muzzle brake is wanted, fit the secondary attachment sold separately — a brake cannot mount to this can directly.
Fire 10 to 15 rounds so the pressure clears debris the cleaning loosened.
fncheck: Sight through the Backcountry from the mount end and confirm one clear channel with no standing solvent — on a welded can that view is the only internal inspection you get. Check the mount is torqued to 50-60 in-lbs and has not come loose in the case. On the rifle, confirm no visible gap at the shoulder, then put the first 10 to 15 rounds through it as Banish's post-clean fouling sequence.
